newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Cargo flights to stay at Schiphol Dutch cabinet told.
newsitem.headline: Cargo flights to stay at Schiphol Dutch cabinet told.

text.p: The Dutch Cabinet has been told there would be little to be gained by decentralising Dutch air cargo or charter operations from the leading Dutch national airport Schiphol.

The Dutch Ministry of Transport commissioned internal research to determine if pressure at the national airport could be eased by moving airlines and their services to other Dutch airports but it concluded the split would undermine Schiphol's role as a hub airport, a spokesman told Reuters.

The Dutch cabinet, however, does want as much small scale traffic as possible diverted to the airport of Lelystad which would have no affect on bigger cargo and charter operations, the official said. The research showed regional airports could do little to absorb Schiphol overspill because of the strong inter-dependence of traffic at the airport.

Three actvities were researched: the possible transfer of business commuter flights; airfreight flights; and charter passenger flights. In all cases, the actvities would be better served at Schiphol the researchers concluded. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
